Hi Matt (and Sara),

Thanks again for the demo today — great questions from your engineering team. I wanted to recap the performance targets we reviewed and hand off the test artifacts so your QA can run the customer-led rehearsal next week. High-level SLOs we agreed on: 

- Latency: generation p95 < 120 ms (end-to-end token generation)
- Streaming: stable streaming latency p95 < 80 ms, max concurrent streaming sessions = 400
- Throughput: steady-state 250 req/s for 30m; acceptable burst to 500 req/s for ≤5m
- Concurrency: up to 1,200 simultaneous short-lived requests (100–200ms), streaming and non-streaming mixed workload

Next steps for the load rehearsal (please confirm):
1) We will provide a k6 script and a Locust recipe — attached is the k6 script (helios-k6-script.js).
2) Please provide a 4-hour test window when your team will run the scripts (we suggested Wed Nov 24, 10:00–14:00 PT).
3) Allowlist our test IPs (see attachment ip_allowlist.txt).
4) Use the test credentials we’ll provision (see test_credentials.csv) and do not run more than 2 unique accounts per simulated user.
5) Confirm whether you’ll run both k6 and Locust; if so, stagger starts by 15 minutes to avoid overshoot at t=0.

Attachments included:
- helios-k6-script.js (k6 scenario, ramp + steady-state)
- ip_allowlist.txt (shortlist of Redwood egress IPs for the rehearsal)
- test_credentials.csv (one-time test tokens + per-team user mapping)

Technical notes for your engineers (short):
- We recommend a 10m linear ramp to steady-state for throughput tests, and a separate streaming probe workload to validate connection churn.
- For streaming tests, set max tokens to 1,000 and a per-session duration of 30s average; this captures KV cache behavior.
- If you need higher KV cache warmup, run a 15m warmup before collecting SLA numbers.

Let us know if the Wed window works; if not we can slide to the following Monday. I’ve CC’d Marissa and she’ll help with allowlist and credential provisioning.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from the runtime team before the rehearsal: 

- KV cache warmup: If you want representative p95 numbers for generation, run a 15-minute warmup at ~30% of steady-state traffic to populate KV caches. Without warmup p95 can be ~10–20% higher on cold runs.
- Batching and quantization: For this test we’ll use the recommended quantization profile (int8) and continuous batching tuned to 12ms batching window; no action required from your side but expect slight variance at burst boundaries.
- Failure modes to watch: 429s during the first 5 minutes of sudden ramp (we’ll track and throttle automatically). If you see sustained 5xxs, abort and notify the on-call (olga@redwood.com).
- Streaming probe: set `max_tokens=1000` and `session_timeout=40s`. For WebSocket runs, use `ping_interval=15s`.
- Temporary scaling: We will temporarily raise the concurrency cap for your tenant for the rehearsal window to ensure we can hit the 500 req/s burst target; this will be reverted after the run.

I’ll be on the call during the run and we will stream server-side traces to your Grafana if you share an endpoint. Looking forward to the test — please send the calendar invite for Sat Nov 27 09:00 ET.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
